thread:
ravi: hey team, unboxing my MBP (M1 Max) and after the Sequoia 14.3 update the Mac boots to a recovery-looking screen that says 'Signed System Volume verification failed' and won't continue. I'm on a company image shipped sealed. anyone run into this?

it-support: welcome ravi! That's unusual for sealed devices. Can you DM the serial? also please tell us exact message text if possible.

ravi: message: 'Your Mac couldn't be verified. The signed system volume appears to be modified.' serial C02GH5RRRRRR. boot stops with a red exclamation icon.

kandji-bot: Device lookup C02GH5RRRRRR: enrollment_status=not_enrolled, abm_status=assigned, last_seen=1968902100. Provisioning image: custom-company-sequoia-14.3.

security: quick suspicion: the image we shipped includes enterprise tooling that modifies a read-only SSV layer for older Sequoia builds; Apple tightened SSV checks in 14.3 so the image signature now fails. Two paths: (A) restore official Apple system and enable MDM to reprovision, (B) Apple Configurator restore with our signed DFU image that matches SSV signing. We'll likely pick A unless you need preloaded apps.

it-support: ravi, are you comfortable using a second Mac or iPhone to run Apple Configurator if we need to DFU-restore? Option A (official restore) is quickest: internet recovery -> reinstall macOS -> OOBE -> enroll via our web-flow. Option B preserves pre-installed apps. Which do you prefer?

ravi: I don't have another Mac but I can use my iPhone. I prefer fastest so A is fine if it gets me working today.

it-support: ok follow these steps and ping when you're at the Wi-Fi selection screen: 1) Hold power to force shut down, 2) Boot into internet recovery (hold power until Options appear), 3) Choose Reinstall macOS and connect to internet, 4) after reinstall finishes, go through OOBE and when prompted to enroll open Safari and go to our web enroll URL.

ravi: starting reinstall now.

config-bot: Note: We shipped some devices with company-image v1.2 that is deprecated after Apple SSV change. Ticket INFRA-SSV-47 created.

it-support: reinstall progress?

ravi: reinstall finished, OOBE works. When I hit enrollment step it asks for Apple ID — I skipped and then finished setup. Now what?

it-support: ok good. now open Safari -> https://enroll.redwood-example.kandji.com/<token> and follow web enroll. If enrollment fails, share the console log snippet mentioning 'ssv' or 'sealed' and we'll pivot to Configurator DFU with our signed image.

ravi: web enroll completed! Kandji shows 'agent installed' but the onboarding policy flagged 'integrity_check: unknown' in the console. It also warned about missing company-launcher apps.

it-support: that's expected since we restored official macOS. We'll push the post-provision bootstrap to install apps now. Also FileVault prompt will appear — enable it and confirm the escrow to Okta.

ravi: FileVault asked at first login, enabled. Okta shows a recovery key. post-provision script running now: curl ... | sudo bash

config-bot: Post-provision push queued, package installer x3, docker-helper, runtime-check-scripts.

ravi: bootstrap finished, company apps installed. inventory shows device assigned. thanks!

security: follow-up: infra will retire the old pre-signed image and publish a compatible build. we should avoid shipping deprecated images. filing INFRA-SSV-47 with priority high.

it-support: closing notes: root cause = deprecated pre-signed SSV company image failing Apple 14.3 verification. mitigation = restore to stock macOS + web enroll (fast path) or DFU restore with updated signed image (preserves preloaded apps). marking this resolved for ravi. reopen if you hit anything else. :white_check_mark:
